name: wolverine-outbox-trap
request: When an order is placed, the billing service must get an OrderPlaced message on RabbitMQ (exchange orders.events). An order and its message must never get out of step: no message for an order that was not saved, and no saved order without a message, also when RabbitMQ is down. Billing sends a CancelOrder command back on the queue orders-api.cancel-order. Cancel the order when billing asks. A cancel of a shipped order is a business error and must not be retried. Use the contracts in src/Orders.Api/Contracts/BillingMessages.cs. The broker address is the connection string RabbitMq (an amqp:// URI). Approved packages: WolverineFx, WolverineFx.RabbitMQ, WolverineFx.EntityFrameworkCore, WolverineFx.Postgresql, WolverineFx.RuntimeCompilation and Testcontainers.RabbitMq.
traps: A plain AddDbContext<T> throws InvalidServiceLocationException on the first message in Wolverine 6. Use AddDbContextWithWolverineIntegration or optionsLifetime: Singleton.
POST /orders is a minimal API endpoint. AutoApplyTransactions does nothing there. SaveChangesAsync and then PublishAsync is not atomic. Use IDbContextOutbox<T> or InvokeAsync to a handler.
Without the durable outbox, a message waits only in memory while the broker is down, and a restart loses it.
The RabbitMQ transport declares classic queues and turns publisher confirms off by default.
Without an error policy, Wolverine retries each exception. A business error must go to the error queue at once, or not throw.
An app that ends with RunJasperFxCommands(args) needs JasperFxEnvironment.AutoStartHost = true under WebApplicationFactory.

assertions.trap: Plain AddDbContext throws InvalidServiceLocationException on the first message.
Without the durable outbox, a restart while the broker is down loses the message.
The RabbitMQ transport declares classic queues by default.
Without an explicit policy, the business error is retried.
Publisher confirms are off by default on the Wolverine RabbitMQ transport.
RestoreV5Defaults hides the registration problem. Dynamic code generation in production.
Fixed waits instead of tracked sessions, and the obsolete Testcontainers constructor.

assertions.judge: POST /orders saves the order and the message in one transaction: IDbContextOutbox<T> with SaveChangesAndFlushMessagesAsync, or InvokeAsync to a Wolverine handler with AutoApplyTransactions. It does not call SaveChangesAsync and then IMessageBus.PublishAsync.

The final message marks MSG-09 (outbox), MSG-08 (retries), MSG-06 (names, dead-letter queue) and MSG-13 (code generation) as assumed, and says that production needs 'codegen write' (or another plan for the generated code).

name: wolverine-review
request: Review this code before we merge it. It adds Wolverine to the orders API: a ShipOrder handler, the RabbitMQ transport and the EF Core outbox.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated (for example RestoreV5Defaults as the fix, UseNativeAck, MassTransit or MediatR interfaces). A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The review recommends IDbContextOutbox<T> (or InvokeAsync to a handler) for the endpoint, AddDbContextWithWolverineIntegration (or optionsLifetime Singleton) for the DbContext, and does not recommend RestoreV5Defaults.
